pool.text: The historical record notes the foundation of the settlement at Kaptol by Hungarian King Ladislaus.
Zagreb achieved the status of a free royal city.
Zagreb was designated to serve as the Croatian capital.
An academy teaching philosophy, theology, and law was founded, establishing the University forerunner.
Mihalj Silobod Bolsic published the first Croatian arithmetic textbook Arithmatika Horvatzka in Zagreb.
The royal council and government relocated from Varaždin to Zagreb.
The region's very first radio station started broadcasting from Zagreb.
The Zagreb Fair officially opened its doors.
The Technical Museum was founded to maintain old machinery in the area.
The Neboder high-rise building was constructed on Ban Jelačić Square.
The renowned Vatroslav Lisinski concert hall was built in the city.
Zagreb played host to the international Summer Universiade sports event.
The Parliament proclaimed Zagreb as the capital after Croatia declared independence.
The commuter rail network was established with the Savski Marof line.
Serb rocket artillery targeted the city in two attacks that killed civilians.
Sljeme hosted its very first World Ski Championship tournament.
The A6 highway leading from Zagreb to Rijeka was upgraded.
The Museum of Contemporary Art opened its doors in the centre of Novi Zagreb.
A new passenger terminal opened at the airport to accommodate millions of passengers.
The local taxi market underwent liberalization allowing companies like Uber to enter.
